subject: Miri (Stacked Borrows and Tree Borrows) over the ssl::ssl_conf tests, and the sensitivity control for the SslConfCtx borrow question

candidate.note: run against the fix commit plus an uncommitted cfg(miri) shim; the shim is committed with this receipt

toolchain.note: the default 1.98.1 toolchain has no miri component; the pinned nightly is selected by RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN and the nightly cargo is invoked directly because the rustup proxy resolves to the default toolchain

shims.why: Miri cannot execute libc foreign calls; CONF_parse_list reached isspace and then strchr before the callback under test was invoked
shims.gating: cfg(miri) only; release and ordinary test builds compile the unchanged sys::* path

semantics.conf_isspace: domain 0..=255; space, tab, LF, VT, FF, CR answer nonzero; 0x80..=0xFF answer 0 in the admitted locale
semantics.conf_strchr: scan for the separator byte, stop at NUL, return null if absent; sep is any non-NUL byte, and a NUL sep returns the terminator, as libc does

control.purpose: prove the instrument fires on the pre-fix borrow shape, so the clean run means something
control.shape_restored: let c = unsafe { &*cctx }; with c.ntbl / c.tbl read across the call into ssl_match_option
control.why: the only path that forms &mut *cctx is a match, and ssl_match_option returns true immediately after ssl_set_option, so ssl_set_option_list returns before any later read of c. The loop iterates again only on non-matches, which never take &mut. Miri reports UB on the use of an invalidated tag, not on the retag itself, so the overlap is never witnessed by these tests.
control.corroboration: a temporary compile_error! in the scratch source fired on the identical invocation, so the runner compiled the scratch source and the result is not a stale-artefact artefact
control.cleanup: scratch tree, logs and target directory removed; repository unchanged by the control

interpretation.what_the_fix_is: a borrow-discipline hardening that removes a latent shared-across-mutable overlap on SslConfCtx
interpretation.what_it_is_not: a confirmed memory-safety defect repair: no executed path used the stale shared reference after the mutable reborrow, so no undefined behaviour was observed, and this receipt does not claim one was
interpretation.corrected_prior_claim: an earlier commit message in this branch described the overlap as UB by the aliasing rules. That overstated the evidence. The overlap violates the discipline that ssl_set_option's # Safety requires, and a later edit could turn it into observable UB, but no test or instrument in this repository has shown the pre-fix code to be unsound at run time.
interpretation.what_the_clean_run_supports: for these four tests, on these paths, under Stacked Borrows and Tree Borrows, with byte-equivalent pure-Rust shims standing in for isspace and strchr, no undefined behaviour was reported

scope_and_non_claims: This is a deep-state / modified-model result: libc is replaced by pure-Rust shims, so the claim is about the Rust code around that boundary, not about libc or authentic execution (AGENTS.md 13).
Four tests, one module, one foreign-call class. No dependency closure, no protocol court, no cryptographic property.
The absence of a Miri diagnostic is not proof of aliasing freedom; the control shows the chosen tests do not witness this particular overlap at all.
A load-bearing control would need a test that reads the shared reference after a successful match, or a table whose match does not short-circuit. That test does not exist and is not claimed.
Miri is not the normative aliasing specification; it is a research instrument and this receipt records what it did and did not cover.
